title: How Your Brain Works
summary: Neurons, memory and why sleep matters: a tour of the control centre of your body.

steps.title: The control centre
sentences: Your brain is the control centre of your body.
It weighs about 1.4 kilograms and is made of around 86 billion tiny cells called neurons.
Neurons talk to each other with tiny electric signals and chemical messages.

steps.title: Parts and jobs
sentences: The big wrinkled top part is the cerebrum, which handles thinking, speaking and planning.
The cerebellum at the back helps with balance and movement.
The brain stem connects to the spinal cord and controls things you do without thinking, such as breathing.

steps.title: Learning changes the brain
sentences: When you practise something, the neurons you use form stronger connections.
That is why practice makes a skill easier, whether it is riding a bicycle or solving a sum.
The brain keeps this ability to change throughout life, which scientists call neuroplasticity.

steps.title: Sleep and memory
sentences: While you sleep, your brain sorts what you learned during the day.
Without enough sleep it is harder to pay attention and to remember things.
Children between about 6 and 12 years usually need nine to twelve hours of sleep.

facts: The brain uses about one fifth of the body's energy, though it is only about two percent of its weight.
Information can travel along some neurons at more than 100 metres per second.
You do not use only ten percent of your brain: nearly all of it is active over a day.

quiz.why: The cerebellum coordinates balance and movement.

quiz.q: Why does practice help you improve?
quiz.why: Repeating something strengthens the pathways used.

quiz.q: About how much sleep do children aged 6 to 12 usually need?
quiz.why: Most children in this age group need 9 to 12 hours.
